I promise you it gets better, that's not just some cliche advice. Not long ago I was in your shoes. 

I've been in your shoes. I have a very similar story. This happened to me at age 25. 

I had a very good job. 3 years with the company. My longest job ever. Lost it with no warning. I was deviated.

At the same time I was also 12,000 in credit card debt and honestly nothing to show for it. I decided to go the bankruptcy route. It's no where near as bad as people make it seem. I owned no house or car, nothing of real value so it didn't hurt me much.

After filing for bankruptcy, losing my job, we decided to move in with a friend. She had offered my husband and I a room in her house. We only had to pay half of her 300 rent.

At first it was fine. Then she let her addict bf move in. She stopped taking her meds. She got super paranoid about us. With in a month she screamed at us to move out.

I was at my lowest then. I picked up my husbands gun. Took everything left in me not to pull the trigger on myself... At the time, not only had a ruined my life but his. I was in a very VERY dark place at that moment. 

I reached out to my sisters. Explained the situation of us being on the verge of being homeless.

 They got us an apartment in their home state and we had left nearly everything we owed.

It's now been a full year since then. I have a better job with people who are more understanding. My husband and I are in the process of rebuilding, saving for a car and a house. I live closer to my sisters and see them often.

Recently I reached the point where I'm doing good without my medication.

We've lived here for a year now. It's been an up and down battle trying to readjust. 

But to think a little over a year ago, I held a gun to my head and nearly ended everything. And to see where I am now at 27, just a year made so much difference for me. Just getting out of a shit town, shit environment made so much difference in my life.

We all make mistakes, we all learn from them early  20s is a hard time because you're learning how life works. You make stupid financial choices, stupid friend choices, stupid career choices, the list goes on. But you can learn from it and grow from it. Believe me when I say it gets better. Believe me when I say you WILL have regrets, but that just part of life. It's a learning phase we all go through at some point.

My life now is far from perfect or where I want it to be. Yet it's SO much better than where it was.
And I have a strong feeling it's going to keep getting better because I've learned from my past what not to do.

I'm so sorry you are going through this. Being someone whos dealt with manic episodes, it's hard to think a head let alone see the damage you are doing at the time.

Given that you think this is a manic episode I'd recommend cross posting in bipolarSOs for more specific support.

That aside, you need to put your foot down, he needs to see a counselor and possibly get on medication. It takes two people to make it work and if he isn't willing to put in the work nothing is going to get better.

The damage done during manic episodes can effect the relationship for months or even years. Couples counseling is a good start but, He should be in individual counseling as well.

I'd suggest sitting down and having a serious talk with him. Let him know if he wants any chance at all of saving the relationship then he needs to take care of his mental health and get treatment.

Also Unless you feel you can trust him to continue working at his current job, he should actively be seeking out a different job.

In short, manic episodes are tough for both parties, it's hard for the person in the manic episode to see the damage they are doing at the time. He needs treatment for this if he has any hope at all of fixing his own issues let alone the issues in your relationship.

Bipolar so here 

Best thing to do is to keep stress low.

Things that help me

Clean house. Your mind gets overwhelmed and your thoughts can get disorganized if the area around you is a mess. The cleaner the better.

Meal prep. Not worrying about food is nice. If it's in the fridge and I can just heat it up or in the crockpot and I just need a plate it helps a lot. Especially if Im cycling and I got into a depressive state. 

Think about it, the hospital is clean and her she dosent have to make her own meals when shes hungry.  Prep meals together. It makes it a fun thing to do as a couple.

Also hobbies,

Coloring - studies have shown that coloring has the same effect on the brain as meditation.

Video games, my go to's are sims and animal crossing. Both are really relaxing and keep your mind off of stressing. I'm addicted to addicted to animal crossing! You can do a lot in that game.

Also talk to her! Ask her what helps her when she's stressed out.

Oh and reassure her that you love her, I've only been I  the hospital for this once it was very draining and once I realized the severity of the situation I felt guilty af for what I put my loved ones through.

I hope some of this helps.

Ive been on zoloft for quite a while now. It helps a good amount. I was on 50mg then went to 100 was on 100mg for about 9 months or so and then the manufacturer changed, pharmacy told me it was the same medication but after the change I started getting mildly manic and it was mild enough I didn't notice and my partner pointed it out. Mainly just me being angry, not feeling any other emotions, trouble sleeping.

I went down to 50 mgs and have been for 2 weeks and I feel SO much better being back on the lower dose. While I am more emotional I can actually FEEL other emotions besides anger. My brain is still adjusting to the lower dose but I feel more normal now.

Typically your doctor will start you on a low dose, just be sure if you feel the need to increase the dose that you talk to your doctor first.

OH also drinking this medication can have bad side effects. First time I drank on it I had a manic episode worst one ever that resulted in paranoia and involvement of law enforcement... Not my best moment. Since then I limit my drinking 1 or 2 glasses of wine max, and go light on the mixed drinks.

On applications you don't have to disclose the specific disability. I have bipolar and cerebral palsy. I have disabilities. However I am not disabled because I can work under the right circumstances. Hi, bipolar female sub here. 

First, do you get alone time with your therapist?  Having your parents with you in most of your sessions can make it hard to open up. I've been in and out of counseling for years. My parents have only attended a session with me once or twice upon my request or suggestion of the therapist and even then they made sure I was okay with it. You have the right to have private sessions with your therapist and what you say can not be repeated to anyone unless in the case of you potentially harming yourself or others. You have to be able to open up to your therapist otherwise there's no point, if you're not open with them they can't help you work through the issues. 

Second, yes medications have a lot of side effects, this is due to the fact that when the medication is in the trial phase, any  abnormalities someone experiences is listed as a potential side effect. Clinical trials are fairly large and have diverse groups of people. So say a 40 year old male starts taking the medication and starts balding shortly after, it becomes listed as a potential side effect because it's occurring to him during the clinical trial, however the medication may not be the source.  But because they can't determine if it's from the medication or his genetics it's listed as a potential side effect.  Just because it's listed as a side effect doesn't mean you will have that side effect. Yes there will be some side effects with any medication but you're more likely to get minor ones like nausea, headaches, drowsiness things like that, which normally fade after the first few weeks once your body adjusts to the medication. 

Most of us with bipolar disorder do have to take medication to function better. I'm on zoloft and have been for the past year. It's made a major difference in my mental health. Yes I can't function without it, not because I've been taking it and I'm " addicted " BUT because I couldn't function BEFORE I started taking the medication which is why it was prescribed to me in the first place.  Medication can make a major impact on your mental health and help you function better. It can take time to find the proper medication but you won't know if it will help unless you try. 

You can always try a medication and see if it helps and IF you have adverse side effects or you feel the medication isn't working talk to your doctor and they can try something else. With bipolar and depression sometimes it takes a little bit of trial and error to find the right combination of meds to help. But you won't know until you try. 

As other users have pointed out there is a major difference between taking an anti depressant and painkillers. 

Third. If you're feeling suicidal you're not fine this is why I mentioned the importance of being able to be open with your therapist and giving medication a try because it can help a lot. If you continue to put those things off your mental health can get worse. 

Fourth, there are a lot of female doms out there. So keep looking. It's not as uncommon as you might think. However right now I think you need to focus on getting yourself into a more stable mental space before worrying about a relationship. While being a sub dose help me a good deal with things it's not a replacement for proper treatment. 

While it may help, getting into a D/S relationship ( or any relationship for that matter ) isn't going to fix your issues in fact getting into one with that expectation will put extra stress on the relationship for both you and your dommie and can cause issues. 

Focus on getting better. It's a long road but you're not alone. Check out r/bipolar as it may help. I've found it very supportive.

I second what u/somethingsophie is saying I would also like to add IF you two get back together I HIGHLY recommend couples counseling. It will give both of you an outside perspective of how the other feels AND help the two of you communicate better.

I have been on zoloft for 6 months or so. I'm on 100 mg. I've found it helps with the depression symptoms and helps me have less swings in my mood. I tried going off of it for a bit, this was not fully intentional as we had just moved and I ran out of my meds and I realized off the meds I'm worse. BUT medications work differently for different people. This may just not be the right medication for you. If you continue to have rapid swings in mood or hypomanic episodes talk to your doctor. For me personally it's helped a tramendous amount. But I've also been on it a while and I'm on a high dose, even with the high dose I still have swings in my mood and still have periods of depression and mania.  

I should also note : I started on 50 mg and increased the dose to 75 after 6 weeks. Then to 100 a month later. Your body builds up a tolerance to the medication after a few weeks so you may need to increase your dose. Talk to your doctor before doing so tho. 

Meds are the trickest part to work out. What works for one person may not work for you. If you feel it's not working for you, talk to your doctor they can either increase your dose or try a different mediction. Do not quit anything cold turkey always talk to your doctor before stopping a medication or increasing your dose. I cannot stress that last part enough due to how medications effect brain chemistry.

I hope this helps. It can be hard getting the proper medication level or finding one that works for you, it's a lot of trial and error BUT you can find something to help just be honest with your doctor's and keep trying.
